title: Barley vs. Oats: Fiber, Protein, and Key Differences

seo.title: Barley vs. Oats: Fiber, Protein, and Key Differences
seo.meta_description: Dry oats and whole barley both provide about 12–14 g protein/100 g; hulled barley can exceed 15 g fiber, while oats stand out for beta-glucan and higher fat.
seo.search_intent: Compare barley and oats for protein, fiber, beta-glucan, fat, and uses.

excerpt: Oats and barley are both beta-glucan-rich grains, but their profiles differ. Dry oats and hulled barley each provide roughly 12–14 g protein per 100 g. Hulled barley can contain much more total fiber, while oats contain more fat and are especially convenient as flakes.
content_html:
Both are fiber-rich grains, but they are not interchangeable. Whole hulled barley usually wins on total fiber; oats combine protein, unsaturated fat, and beta-glucan in a particularly convenient breakfast grain.

Compare them dry

Dry rolled oats commonly provide around 13 g protein and 10 g fiber per 100 g. Hulled whole barley is roughly 12–13 g protein and can exceed 15 g fiber.

Pearled barley is different: polishing removes some bran, so it contains less fiber and is not equivalent to intact hulled barley.

Both provide beta-glucan

Beta-glucan is a viscous soluble fiber found in both oats and barley. These grains are the best-known cereal sources.

Oats contain more fat

Oats are relatively high-fat for a cereal, often around 6–7 g per 100 g dry, mostly unsaturated. Barley is much lower.

Uses

Oats dominate porridge, muesli, granola, and baking. Barley works well in soups, stews, salads, and malt products.

For total fiber, whole barley; for a higher-fat, protein-rich breakfast grain, oats.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: They are similar dry, generally around 12–14 g per 100 g.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Whole hulled barley usually has more total fiber, while pearled barley has less because of polishing.

faq.question: Do both contain beta-glucan?
faq.answer: Yes. Oats and barley are major dietary sources of beta-glucan.
